title: Colony PCR with Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 and Gel Electrophoresis
author: Maximilian Dietsch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.mk5c4y6

steps.title: Prepare colony suspension
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl nuclease‑free sterile water to a tube and inoculate it with material from a fresh, light‑green colony taken from an agar plate; work under sterile conditions.

steps.title: Lyse cells by heat
steps.instruction: Heat the suspension at 95 °C for 10 minutes; handle the hot tube with care.

steps.title: Pellet debris by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the heated sample at 13 000 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Assemble PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a master mix for each reaction using the DreamTaq DNA Polymerase Kit (Thermo Fisher): add 2 µl 10× DreamTaq buffer, 0.4 µl dNTP mix, 2 µl forward primer, 2 µl reverse primer, 0.2 µl DreamTaq polymerase, and nuclease‑free water (12.4 µl if the template volume will be 1 µl, or 12.3 µl if the template volume will be 2 µl) to give a total of 18–19 µl. Alternatively, use the Thermo Fisher DreamTaq Master Mix (which already contains buffer, dNTPs, and polymerase) and add the forward primer, reverse primer, template DNA, and water as instructed in the kit leaflet.

substeps.instruction: Add each component in the order listed.
Mix gently and keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Combine master mix with template
steps.instruction: Pipette 18–19 µl of the prepared master mix into a PCR tube containing 1–2 µl of the colony‑lysis supernatant (template).

steps.title: Run PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler as follows (35 cycles): 1) Initial denaturation 98 °C for 2 min; 2) Denaturation 98 °C for 30 s; 3) Annealing 58 °C (5 °C below the lowest primer Tm of 63 °C) for 30 s; 4) Extension 72 °C for 1 min (extend 1 min per kb, up to 2 kb); 5) Final extension 72 °C for 10 min; hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1% agarose gel
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.5 g agarose and dissolve it in 50 ml 1× TAE buffer; microwave at 360 W until the solution is clear. Cool to lukewarm (still touchable, not hot) while gently shaking to avoid lumps. Add 2.5 µl midoriGreen Advance (1 : 20 000 dilution) and mix. Pour the gel into a casting tray, insert the comb, allow to harden, then remove the comb and fill the gel chamber with 1× TAE buffer until the gel is fully soaked.

substeps.instruction: Weigh agarose and add to buffer.
Let gel solidify, then remove comb.

steps.title: Add loading dye to PCR products
steps.instruction: Add 4 µl of 6× loading dye (Thermo Fisher) to each PCR tube and mix gently.

steps.title: Mix samples with dye and load gel
steps.instruction: Pipette each dyed PCR sample up and down to mix, then load the appropriate volume into the wells of the hardened agarose gel. Pipette 5 µl of GeneRuler 1 kb Plus DNA ladder (ready‑to‑use) into a separate well as size reference.

steps.title: Electrophorese gel
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 120 V, monitoring the dye front until it reaches approximately two‑thirds of the gel length.

steps.title: Image gel
steps.instruction: Visualize the gel using a Bio‑Rad ChemyDoc MP system with the GelGreen channel in Image Lab 5.0 software; midoriGreen Advance fluorescence will reveal DNA bands.

steps.title: Store remaining PCR supernatant
steps.instruction: Pipette 1–2 µl of the supernatant into a fresh PCR tube; freeze the remaining sample (including the pellet) at –20 °C. When needed, thaw at room temperature, centrifuge at 13 000 rpm for 1 minute, and pipette 1–2 µl of the supernatant for a subsequent colony PCR.
